children: Indian government bonds are likely to extend losses in early deals on Tuesday, tracking a spike in U.S. Treasury yields after fresh military escalation between Iran and the U.S.

The yield on the benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) is expected to trade between 6.94% and 6.99%, a trader at a private bank said, after closing at 6.9452%, the highest since June 8, in the previous session.

U.S. forces struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday, while Iran responded by attacking U.S. forces stationed in Jordan, according to media reports. Persistently high crude oil prices triggered by the war, now entering its seventh month, have stoked inflation and pushed up yields as investors brace for rate hikes from the Fed.
"Bearish factors globally are putting relentless pressure on bonds," the trader said.
ending above the 4.75% handle for the first time since January 2025, before extending its rise further in Asian trading hours.

Market wagers on the likelihood of a 25 basis point hike by the Fed later this month have jumped to 66%, up from around 41% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The shift followed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech in which he indicated the Fed may have to hike if inflation does not ease toward its 2% target.

The benchmark Brent crude contract stayed around $91 per barrel, putting pressure on large importers like India, as a sustained rise in crude prices could worsen its inflation and government finances.

Meanwhile, the Indian economy grew 7.8% on-year in April-June, above the 7.1% estimate in a Reuters poll, adding to the potential for the Reserve Bank of India to move towards monetary policy tightening.
India's overnight indexed swap rates could touch fresh highs in line with bond yields.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) swap rate ended at 6.00%, and the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) closed at 6.1850%. The most liquid five-year rate (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) settled at 6.4825%.
